record.title: ScienceBuddy reports gains from co-evolving a scientific-task harness and language model
record.summary: Li et al. describe a recursive-in-recursive process that edits an execution harness and trains a task model over three cycles. On their task-ID-held-out scientific-task benchmark, the authors report single-attempt accuracy rising from 42.2% to 73.3%, with 33.3% of cases changing from incorrect to correct and 2.2% from correct to incorrect. The measurements are author-reported benchmark outcomes, not verified scientific discoveries. The linked repository’s maintained preview uses a different task inventory and experiment configuration from the paper case study, so it does not independently validate those values.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The inspected paper describes a three-cycle recursive-in-recursive procedure that edits an execution harness and trains a task model, with a fixed GPT-6 Astra editor helper in the reported case study.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On the paper’s task-ID-held-out benchmark, authors report single-attempt scientific-task accuracy increasing from 42.2% to 73.3%; 33.3% of cases change from incorrect to correct and 2.2% from correct to incorrect, across four task families.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: For a standalone harness adaptation experiment with a fixed model, authors report validation accuracy increasing from 31.1% to 51.1% after 24 batches comprising 288 simulated adaptation conversations; a separate fixed-harness pass@4 coverage measure rises from 48.3% to 67.8%.

claims.label: SPECULATIVE
claims.text: The results establish that ScienceBuddy makes scientific discoveries or broadly improves scientific productivity in real research settings.

contradictory_evidence: The paper evaluates task completion and benchmark answers; its results do not establish scientific discoveries or validate the truth of generated research outcomes.

The authors’ currently maintained repository preview uses a different task inventory and experiment configuration than the paper case study. The public code inspected therefore does not independently reproduce the reported paper values.

evidence_gaps.description: The current public repository documents a maintained preview that differs from the paper case-study configuration. This review did not inspect an exact paper code/config/data snapshot, raw logs or weights that bind the reported 42.2%→73.3% result to an executable artifact.
Benchmark task accuracy measures task completion, not whether a system produced a valid scientific discovery or useful result in a live research workflow.
All quantitative outcomes reviewed are author-reported; the research desk did not independently execute the system.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported gain generalizes to independent scientific tasks with outcome validation, recursive co-adaptation of a model and its research harness could improve research-task execution. A 5 reflects a potentially field-shaping method with evidence from one author-run benchmark and no demonstrated discoveries or independent replication.
limitations: Quantitative results are author-reported and were not independently reproduced.
The reported task benchmark covers four task families and measures benchmark task answers rather than verified scientific discoveries or downstream research impact.
The paper’s case study uses a fixed GPT-6 Astra editor helper and a Qwen3.5-4B task model; broader model and editor transfer is unknown.

The paper’s 895-task collection and reported adaptation protocol are not bound in this review to the currently maintained repository experiment. The repository preview uses a different 715/90/90 inventory and different cycle, search-step and RL-update settings.

Validation selection and material-group overlap across train/test described in the repository weaken interpretation of test independence for the maintained preview; those preview results must not be conflated with paper plots.
Improved benchmark task performance does not establish that the system made valid discoveries or improved real research outcomes.
brief.summary: Li et al. describe a recursive-in-recursive process that edits an execution harness and trains a task model over three cycles. On their task-ID-held-out scientific-task benchmark, the authors report single-attempt accuracy rising from 42.2% to 73.3%, with 33.3% of cases changing from incorrect to correct and 2.2% from correct to incorrect. The measurements are author-reported benchmark outcomes, not verified scientific discoveries. The linked repository’s maintained preview uses a different task inventory and experiment configuration from the paper case study, so it does not independently validate those values.

technical.claimed_result: Authors report task-ID-held-out single-attempt accuracy of 42.2% before and 73.3% after three cycles across four task families; 33.3% of benchmark cases change from incorrect to correct and 2.2% from correct to incorrect. In a separate fixed-model harness adaptation case, validation accuracy is reported as 31.1%→51.1% after 24 batches/288 simulated conversations; fixed-harness pass@4 coverage is reported as 48.3%→67.8%.
technical.demonstrated_result: The paper describes the training procedure and reports the stated benchmark outcomes. the research desk inspected but did not execute the implementation or reproduce the values.
technical.implementation_status: A public author repository is available. Its maintained science-buddy-preview experiment is explicitly different from the paper case-study plots/configuration, so the current repository does not establish exact reproduction of the paper results.
technical.mechanism: Across three cycles, a fixed editor helper searches for harness changes while a task model is updated with reinforcement learning; the paper frames the process as recursive co-evolution of the execution harness and task model.
technical.regime: One author-run case study with Qwen3.5-4B as task model and GPT-6 Astra as fixed editor helper; three co-evolution cycles; four scientific-task families; task-ID-held-out benchmark. Separate fixed-model harness adaptation uses 24 batches and 288 simulated conversations.
technical.reproducibility: The current public repository documents a distinct maintained preview configuration (715/90/90 tasks, three cycles, three harness search steps, 16 training interactions per step, three proposals per step, 30 RL updates per stage). It does not bind that configuration to the paper plots. Exact paper snapshot, raw logs and independent replay remain unverified.
technical.strongest_baseline: The reported headline comparison is the initial task-model/harness system at 42.2% single-attempt accuracy versus 73.3% after three co-evolution cycles; this is an author-reported within-study comparison, not an independent benchmark.

brief.title: ScienceBuddy reports gains from co-evolving a scientific-task harness and language model
brief.why_it_matters: If replicated on independently authored scientific tasks with outcome checks, co-evolving a research execution harness and its task model could improve task completion. The current evidence establishes a bounded author-run benchmark result; it does not show that the system made scientific discoveries or that the currently maintained repository reproduces the paper case study.
